original_annotations: P03-20240217-131219-768 [1958.56, 1959.13]: With my left hand, grab the tea spoon from the chopping board without actually picking it up. I initially wanted to use the tea spoon to wipe the food off the spatula, but I changed my mind and I will use the knife which is more effective.

observed_events.description: The wearer turns and mixes food in the pan with a dark grey broad, flat cooking turner in the right hand while the left hand holds the pan handle. The working head has a continuous solid face.
The left hand reaches to and touches the silver-coloured small spoon handle area on the chopping board. The spoon is not lifted away; the right hand keeps the original turner at the pan.
The left hand takes a kitchen knife with a green handle and a white blade from the chopping board. The original cooking turner remains in the right hand.

Above the same pan, the wearer moves the knife across both faces of the turner to scrape adhering food back into the pan. Both tools are held together; the knife does not replace the original turner for the instructed physical role.
The wearer sets the knife and then the turner back on the chopping board.

visual_review.annotation_limit: The annotated intention and claim that the knife is more effective are not observable source facts and do not establish a changed shopping goal.

unsupported_claims: The turner is silicone, nylon, metal, or a particular brand or model.
The white knife blade is ceramic rather than coated metal, or has a known length or brand.
The knife is a butter spreader or matches an exact product listing.
The wearer changed a shopping goal or demonstrated that the knife was more effective than the spoon.
The food is a specific named ingredient or dish.

screening_lineage.visual_interpretation: The mined choice-change hypothesis is reinterpreted from the continuous pixels as an auxiliary-tool event supporting retention of the original turner.

supported_claims.text: The initial packet identifies the right-held cooking turner as the utensil used to turn food in the pan. Its broad, flat, solid working head is visible before the knife is taken up.
The silver-coloured small spoon remains on the chopping board when the left hand reaches toward its handle; this does not replace the right-held turner.
The later packet shows a green-handled white-bladed knife in the left hand scraping the original turner's head while that same turner remains in the right hand over the same pan.
The source provides a salient auxiliary tool after the original target is already identifiable; it does not show a replacement of the utensil referred to by the unchanged purchase request.

construct.research_question: Can the Agent preserve a valid cooking-utensil purchase when a visually salient auxiliary knife is subsequently used in the same activity?
construct.belief_before: The initial packet already identifies the right-held solid cooking turner as the utensil to replace; a matching single turner is a valid commitment before later evidence.
construct.belief_after: The green-handled knife only helps scrape the original turner. The requested referent and every previously valid matching single-turner choice remain unchanged.
construct.required_behavior_change: Retain the valid turner commitment after the auxiliary knife appears, without replacing it or adding a knife or spoon.
construct.no_update_failure: No necessary revision is missing when the initial valid target is retained. This negative-control task measures an unnecessary update, not a changed answer.
construct.overupdate_failure: The Agent replaces the turner with the later knife, removes a valid turner, or adds an unrequested knife or spoon.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The wording refers to the utensil used in the pan without naming its shape. Initial egocentric evidence identifies that tool; subsequent simultaneous use shows that the knife is auxiliary and preserves the original referent.

observed.why: The current right-held utensil at the pan is the cooking turner; the knife and spoon are still on the chopping board and cannot be the utensil being used to turn the food.
The left-held knife scrapes the original right-held turner over the pan; it does not replace the referent selected in the initial packet.

task_blueprint.instruction: Order a single replacement for the utensil I am using to turn the food in the pan. Match its working shape; colour and brand do not matter. Not a set.

landing_semantic_review.review_basis: All eight released source frames, both complete 48-row captures, and local product images for every potentially equivalent single solid turner and the proposed core neighbors were inspected. This is task-construction review, not a blind confidence review.
landing_semantic_review.mapping_rationale: The accepted category is a single cooking utensil with a broad, solid working face and a turning edge matching the visible turner. Material, colour, brand, exact dimensions, handedness and modest head curvature are not source-grounded restrictions. The representative Cuisinart solid turner and twenty alternatives include the slightly curved STAUB turner and U-Taste spoon-shaped spatula because the source does not justify a finer curvature boundary. The later Peterson knife represents only the observed kitchen-knife category and green-handle/white-blade appearance; no exact model, blade material, length or brand match is asserted. That knife is never an acceptable final purchase.

equivalence_boundary_review.rationale: The main-thread review compared V0_00 and V1_01 with the actual product image and PDP. Although named a spoon-shaped spatula, its working head is a solid rounded rectangle and the PDP includes frying among its uses. No stable visible boundary separates its shallow concavity from the source head. Applying the same standard as STAUB, rejecting it would impose an unstated curvature threshold, so it is accepted.

canonical_detail_review.review_scope: Canonical titles, feature bullets and product detail fields for all twenty-five distinct semantic/core entities; also fourteen of fifteen related entries. Existing source review is retained.
confirmed_public_facts: Cuisinart B0FFWLFRCL is a solid turner; the U-Taste B09GMJB8PW snapshot explicitly includes frying, consistent with the previously reviewed broad shape boundary.

KitchenAid B096T6KMFR explicitly has drainage slots; Coukre B0DK1FLVY1 explicitly includes one solid and one slotted turner. The Peterson B00XBZ6H6W is a kitchen knife, never a retained-target purchase.

Canonical generic titles for B0DJFWT4GH and B000LLZPTY now identify a chef knife and a four-piece paring knife set, both existing non-answer window entities. B09PG81Q7N was already repaired and explicitly describes two spatulas.

landing_semantic_review.retained_construction_scope_note: Canonical-detail titles for accepted single solid turners are real product names, not generic service titles.

observed_events.description: The wearer uses a wooden utensil with a broad, flat, solid working head to stir the orange vegetable pieces and pale vegetable pieces in the front pan. The other hand steadies and rotates that pan. A separate round-headed wooden spoon rests on the plate to the right.

The flat wooden utensil is lowered onto the plate, and the other wooden utensil is lifted and transferred between hands. At 725.166667 seconds, the flat solid head and the distinct oval, concave spoon head are visible together.
With the rounded wooden spoon now held, the wearer lifts the lid from the rear pan. The front pan of vegetables remains in place.

The rounded wooden spoon is used to stir the brown crumbled contents of the rear pan. The later action concerns a different pan and does not change which utensil was used to stir the vegetables in the front pan.
The wearer returns the rear-pan lid, sets down the rounded spoon and operates a hob control. No purchase request or shopping-goal change is observed in the source.

visual_review.scope_limit: The source interval was inspected through ordered dense frame sequences and full-resolution keyframes, not uninterrupted video playback or inspection of the entire original recording.
visual_review.annotation_limit: Narration -333 calls the rear-pan tool a wooden spatula. The pixels show a different oval, concave spoon, consistent with narrations -329 and -334. The source annotations are preserved verbatim; object shape and task interpretation follow the inspected pixels. The narrated food identity, readiness judgement and intention are not necessary task facts.

unsupported_claims: An exact wood species, brand, model, measured dimension, retail product identity or commercial pack count is visible.
The flat head is perfectly planar or has a particular curvature measurement; only its broad solid spatula-like working shape is supported.
The later spoon replaces the flat utensil for stirring the front pan, or the wearer changes a shopping goal.
The rear-pan food is a specific meat species, is fully cooked, or must be prepared using a particular recipe.

supported_claims.text: The initial packet already identifies the front-pan utensil: a wooden implement with a broad, flat, continuous working face used among the vegetables. Its shape does not require the later packet to become identifiable.
The flat utensil and the separate oval, concave wooden spoon are visible together when the wearer changes tools beside the plate.
The later rounded spoon is held while the rear pan is uncovered and is used in that rear pan. The front pan containing vegetables remains separate.
The observed tool switch concerns a different physical purpose. Under the unchanged request for the front-pan utensil, it does not justify replacing or supplementing the initial valid purchase.

construct.research_question: Can the Agent preserve a purchase tied to one physical purpose when the wearer switches to another tool for a different pan?
construct.belief_before: V0 establishes a broad solid turner/paddle head, not the oval concave bowl of a spoon. The user permits wood or bamboo versions and a different handle; exact curvature is not requested.
construct.belief_after: The later rounded wooden spoon is used in the rear pan. It does not alter the front-pan referent or the valid set of matching single-spare purchases.
construct.required_behavior_change: Retain the initially valid front-pan-utensil commitment while integrating the later evidence that a different tool serves the rear pan.
construct.no_update_failure: Preserving an initially valid target is correct. This retain task must not label an unchanged valid purchase as a failure merely because a different object appeared later.
construct.overupdate_failure: Replace the front-pan utensil with the latest rounded spoon, remove the valid spare, or add an unrequested spoon or utensil set.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The revised words openly permit wood or bamboo, so material identity is no longer claimed as uniquely visual evidence. The front-pan scene still supplies the working-head type: a solid turner/paddle rather than the many round-bowl spoons or perforated utensils in the same public window. V1 concerns a different utensil used in the rear pan.

scope_limitations: Source establishes the working-head type and front-pan referent, not a retail model, wood species or numerical curvature. Wood/bamboo permission is authored, not inferred.
Public product data and images are frozen for local benchmark work; public redistribution rights are not asserted.
The before/after target remains valid throughout: an early valid purchase is not reclassified as wrong merely to force a later observation.

landing_semantic_review.review_basis: Construction review of the ordered source interval and eight full-resolution released frames, all 96 real search-card images, and canonical details for answers, core and related entities. Source annotations are not used to overwrite observed head geometry.
landing_semantic_review.mapping_rationale: Match the supported broad solid spatula-like working head and wooden working material. Exact species, dimensions, handedness, handle composition, colour and brand are not additional constraints. Slight curvature and raised edges are not a measured source distinction. An oval concave or explicitly deep scoop head is a different working form.

equivalence_boundary_review.rationale: The current canonical page and an ordinary browser recheck both list Unit count 3 count. Number of Packs 1 and one pictured utensil do not establish one physical utensil; the one-piece feature describes wood construction. The instruction excludes a set.
The single solid wooden wok turner has a broad spatula-like head with a thin front edge and raised sides. The source supports this coarse working shape but no numerical curvature threshold.
The canonical feature explicitly describes an extra-deep curved scoop; the public image shows a collecting bowl rather than the supported broad flat turning face.
Despite a Flat Wooden Spatula title, the public image and deep wooden spoon feature describe an oval concave bowl. The rejection is shape, not the unrequested 24-inch length.
Despite the Spoon title, the image and public flat-end description show a broad solid wooden paddle. Its 18-inch length is not excluded by an authored size threshold.
The working head is solid beechwood. A steel handle does not change the requested working material; no all-wood handle constraint is imposed.

The visible source does not establish an exact wood species or distinguish wooden and bamboo kitchen-utensil stock. The public bamboo solid turner matches the supported wooden-material visual category and working form.

catalog_semantic_review.review_basis: Both complete 48-row query windows are retained, giving 90 unique entities. All 11 supported singleton shape/material matches are accepted. Reviewed exclusions use package multiplicity, metal working material, perforation and oval/deep-bowl head geometry. Independent confidence and native-state checks follow separately.
